_meta.what_this_is: Two adjacent RGBA pixels straddling the edge of an opaque red shape on a transparent canvas, averaged into one pixel (a 2x downsample of the edge). Each pixel is [r, g, b, a] in [0,1]. The left pixel is opaque red; the right is fully transparent with its color stored as black (the usual default -- a transparent pixel's color is undefined, so tools store 0). The trap: averaging the straight (non-premultiplied) color blends the invisible black of the transparent pixel into the visible color, giving a dark red fringe. Premultiplying first (color *= alpha) removes it, recovering full red.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. Hand-authored RGBA values so the edge color under each method is exact and checkable.
_meta.format: row [[r,g,b,a], ...] (the pixels to average into one)
